standard_prerequisites.name: The definition of a nowhere dense subset as one whose closure has empty interior, and the behaviour of closures under finite unions
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Set up in the author's section on nowhere dense sets, immediately before the counted statement
standard_prerequisites.use: Fixes the notion to be preserved and the identity used in the proof.

core_obligations: Reduction to two sets: since the general case follows by induction, the proof treats two nowhere dense subsets (proof lines 4228-4229).
Closure of the union: the proof uses that the closure of a union is the union of the closures (proof lines 4230).

Empty interior: an open subset of the closure of the union meets each of the two closures in an open set, and nowhere density of each piece forces those to be empty, so the interior of the closure of the union is empty (proof lines 4231-4235).
Conclusion: the union is nowhere dense, and the finite case follows by induction (proof line 4235).
proof_roadmap: 归结为两个集合（一般情形由归纳）。
用 cl(A ∪ B) = cl(A) ∪ cl(B)：若 cl(A∪B) 有非空开子集，则它与 cl(A)、cl(B) 的交分别是各自闭包中的非空开子集，与 A、B 无处稠密矛盾。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the stability of nowhere density under finite unions (author lemma at source lines 4221-4225, label lemma-nowhere-dense). The proof (source lines 4227-4236) reduces to the case of two sets by induction and then argues with the closure identity: an open subset of the closure of the union would meet each closure in an open subset, contradicting the nowhere density of the two pieces (proof lines 4230-4235). The statement is used in the section's treatment of open dense subsets and Baire-type properties. H2.
